title: Annotatio VI §.III (3): Augustine/Zeno — outside Christ they eat sacrament unto condemnation
pass_a_gloss: (3) Concerning all the same — those communicating unworthily who by their malice and wickedness are placed outside Christ’s communion, yet nevertheless communicate at the Lord’s table — that they eat eternal ruin to themselves, testimonies of Augustine and of many other Fathers stand. Thus again Augustine: He who does not abide in Christ, and Christ in him, does not eat his flesh spiritually and drink his blood, even if visibly and carnally he presses with the teeth — not Christ’s body and blood — but the Sacrament of Christ’s Body and Blood, or rather eats and drinks the Sacrament of so great a thing unto condemnation. Whom Zeno of Verona, Origen’s contemporary, foreshadowed: There is cause to fear, he says, that he in whom the Devil dwells does not eat the Lord’s flesh nor drink his Blood, even if he seem to communicate with the faithful — since the Lord’s words so hold: Who eats my flesh and drinks my Blood, he abides in me and I in him.
pass_b_english: (3) Those outside Christ’s communion by malice who still take the Lord’s table eat eternal ruin to themselves — so Augustine and many Fathers.

Augustine: without abiding in Christ they do not eat spiritually, even if teeth press the sacrament unto condemnation. Zeno of Verona: the one in whom the Devil dwells does not eat the Lord’s flesh, though he seem to communicate with the faithful (Jn 6).
source_text: (3) De iisdem omnibus, seu indignè communicantibus, qui per malitiam suam & improbitatem extra communionem Christi positi, nihilominus mensæ Domini communicant, eos sibi æternum exitium comedere, & Augustini, & multorum aliorum Patrum testimonia exstant. Ita enim denuo Augustinus: Ille qui non in Christo manet, & Christus in illo, non edit spiritualiter carnem ejus & sanguinem ejus bibit, etiamsi visibiliter & carnaliter dentibus premat, (non, corpus Christi & sanguinem) sed Sacramentum Corporis & Sang. Christi, seu potius edit & bibit Sacramentum tantæ rei, in condemnationem. Cui prælusit Zeno Veronensis, Origini coævus: Verendi causa est, ait, eum, in quo Diabolus habitat, non edere carnem Domini, nec bibere ejus Sanguinem, etiamsi videatur cum fidelibus communicare: Quandoquidem verba Domini ita habent: Qui manducat carnem meam & bibit Sanguinem meum, ille in me manet & ego in ipso.
